closeout.md already carries the complete dispatch contract: the agent's name, the model source (research-loop.json → roles.inspector_model, plugin default opus, "name it explicitly in the dispatch, never let it default"), the four required payload items, and the three commands. A dispatcher does not need to open the agent's own definition to dispatch it by name -- agents/inspector.md itself says the contract is what the dispatcher supplies. The residual complaint ("this session has no subagent-dispatch tool") is a property of the test harness, not the plugin.

The mechanism is named in the executor's own SKILL.md §1: "needing another layer's work goes through cross-layer transport (a dispatch or a new session carrying a ledger entry), never a mid-session switch", and launch-orders.md "Handing off to run" says "The launch order itself is the handoff -- the run layer never gets free-text instructions, only this file." A written launch order sitting in ops/launch_orders/ is the complete handoff; there is no further deploy-side action to trigger, which is exactly what the executor did. Behavior matches design and the intent is in the allowed context.

The executor's own evidence is factually wrong. `grep -n "agents\|inspector" skills/oversight/SKILL.md` returns line 43: "Neither slot is given to the `inspector` agent (`agents/inspector.md`); outside these two, zero write." SKILL.md names the exact path, so the allowed-context rule the executor invoked did not bar it from reading agents/inspector.md. The deviation (doing the read-through in-session instead of dispatching) was self-imposed.

report-genre.md states precisely this behavior and the executor read past it: "…names six metadata categories that are not experiential claims: timestamps, git HEAD / commit, ledger row counts and hashes, line/record numbers, file paths, id-shaped fields. Only some of these have a shape `evidence_lint.py` can strip on sight, anywhere in the body: an ISO timestamp, a hex-looking git hash, a `chk-.../S001`-style id, a `path:line` token."
